title: Owner console steps need absolute values, and search-console status is checked against the served artifact
trigger: 2026-10-27/29: the agent told the Owner to submit the sitemap as "sitemap.xml" on a Search Console Domain property; it was refused as "Invalid sitemap address". With the absolute URL it was accepted but showed "Couldn't fetch" / type Unknown on the day of submission. Reading the served robots.txt during the check showed a Cloudflare managed group, prepended at the edge, that disallows about 40 AI crawlers, which the source route src/pages/robots.txt.ts does not contain.
root_cause: The handoff was written from memory of the URL-prefix property flow instead of the property type actually in use, and robots/sitemap checks read the source route, while the edge provider rewrites the served file.
rule: A console step handed to the Owner gives the exact absolute value and the expected result for that property type, and search-engine status is diagnosed from the served artifact (URL Inspection live test, served robots.txt and sitemap) before any source change.
reuse_boundary: Search Console, Bing Webmaster and similar Owner-run provider consoles, and any file an edge provider may rewrite (robots.txt, headers). Not a reason to change source when the served file is correct; a first-day "Couldn't fetch" alone is not evidence of a site defect.

guard.path: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-24-seo-ads-marketing-readiness.md section 6, "Before the first ad (Owner)" items 4 and 5
guard.judgment_only_reason: The failing surfaces are Owner-run provider consoles and a Cloudflare dashboard setting; CI cannot read either, and the served robots.txt is rewritten at the edge after the build, so no source test can observe it.
